input.title: How Did the Nepal Flood Happen? | Glacier Collapse Explained | 2D Animation Documentary
input.description:
On August 26, 2026, a devastating natural disaster struck Nepal’s Himalayan region. But how did a glacier and mountain collapse turn into a massive flood?

In this 2D Animation Documentary, we explore the chain of events behind the disaster — from the collapse of ice and rock to the sudden flood of water, debris, and mud through the mountain valleys.

We’ll also examine the role of glacier instability, landslides, rising temperatures, and climate change, and why scientists are closely watching the changing Himalayan landscape.

How did it happen? What triggered the flood? And could something similar happen again?

Watch the full documentary to understand the story behind one of the Himalayas’ most frightening natural disasters.

This documentary is created for educational and informational purposes based on available reports and scientific information. Disaster figures and scientific assessments may change as investigations continue.

audio.transcript_summary: Speaker narrates in Hindi that on 26 August 2026 around 9:30 am in the Trishuli Valley (Trishuli Ghati) of Rasuwa district on Nepal's northern border all was calm as usual with snow on mountain tops and the river flowing normally. He says no one knew nature was about to show its cruelest form. In the Himalaya near Langtang Lirung a huge thousand-year-old ice wall had been weakening unnoticed, with geologists attributing it to warming causing ice to melt, ground to loosen and unseen cracks. That morning the wall near Langtang Lirung suddenly broke causing a massive landslide that shook the mountain, recorded as magnitude 5.2 by seismographs in America and Germany though it was not an earthquake.
